newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Wall Street leads European stocks higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Wall Street leads European stocks higher.

text.p: European stock markets rose strongly on Wednesday as Wall Street led a collective sigh of relief that the U.S. Federal Reserve decided against raising interest rates, for the moment at least.
The dollar, battered overnight by the unchanged interest rates, firmed after a robust U.S. trade report but then was hit by U.S. comments on the sensitive issue of trade relations with Japan.

European share markets were already firm in the morning after the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the policy arm of the U.S. central bank, said after the Tuesday close in Europe that its Fed Funds rate would remain unchanged.

Wall Street then continued a rally which began after the FOMC announcement, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 31.73 points or 0.43 percent at 7,335.19 after half an hour's trade on Wednesday.
This gave European shares a further boost, despite some qualms among investors that the Fed had only postponed an interest rate rise until the summer.

Germany, which fell sharply on jitters before the FOMC meeting on Tuesday, was the biggest beneficiary. The DAX index, which closes before Wall Street opens, finished up 52.66 points or 1.49 percent at 3,596.09. The rise was more dramatic in electronic trade after the floor session, where the IBIS index surged 2.37 percent to 3,599.55.
"If everything looked negative yesterday, it all looks positive now," said a Frankfurt trader.
Initial buying was by traders wrong-footed by the decision to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged. But later keen buying interest emerged, albeit focused on stocks in the news.
Metals and chemicals firm Degussa AG remained among the favourites after utility Veba AG announced plans to buy a large stake in it at well above market value.
Degussa rose 8.80 marks to 84.80 marks, below the Veba buy price of 86.80 marks. Veba was up 90 pfennigs at 99.70.
In London the FTSE 100 index of blue chips gained 45.9 points or 1.0 percent to 4,653.4 by mid afternoon.

This was despite lingering worries that the FOMC, by delaying an interest rate hike now, would have to raise them by half a percentage point when it next meets in July, rather than the quarter point which some analysts had expected on Tuesday.
"The market is riding this good news at the moment. We could see the FTSE hit a new high in the next few days," one senior dealer said. "But it may end in tears in July."
"In some respects, it may have been better for the market if the Fed had tightened yesterday," another dealer said. "The closer we get to the next FOMC meeting, the more the uncertainty will grow."
Concerns are also focused on British rates before the new Labour government's first budget.

News of a slowdown in British broad money supply growth in April eased fears that the Bank of England might push up interest rates before Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's first budget speech.
Although no official date has been set, Brown is widely expected to unveil his spending plans on June 10.

M4 grew by 10.4 percent in the year to April, still well above the three-to-nine percent monitoring range adopted by the previous government but far below the 11.3 percent growth economists were forecasting.
The Paris market was also firmer following the Fed decision, with the CAC 40 index up 39.79 points or 1.44 percent at 2,790.84.
On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar fell below 114 yen after U.S. Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich referred on Wednesday to the trade frictions between Washington and Tokyo.

Ehrlich said Japan should not revert to the past pattern of export-led growth. He was speaking after news that the U.S. trade deficit fell 19.3 percent in March to $8.5 billion but the U.S. defciit with Japan rose 8.3 percent.
The dollar was at 113.85 yen after climbing above 114 following an overnight tumble due to the unchanged interest rates. But it was little changed from 113.80 at the European close on Tuesday.
The dollar was at 1.6937 marks after closing in Europe on Tuesday at 1.6953 and hitting a low later of just above 1.67.

Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick said he had little objection to dollar/mark around 1.70 but there was no need to expect further weakness of the mark against the dollar. The dollar eased only slighly on the remarks.
"What he said was a bit mixed so the market is a bit confused and taking it marginally negatively," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London.

The mark climbed above a 6-1/2 month low against the Swiss franc after the Swiss National Bank announced it would pump liquidity into the market. It stood at 83.16 Swiss centimes from an overnight low of 82.39.
STOCK PRICES AT 1400 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 45.9 points or 1.0 percent to 4,653.4 by mid afternoon.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 39.79 points or 1.44 percent at 2,790.84.
Frankfurt's DAX index was closed up 52.66 points or 1.49 percent at 3,596.09. In later electronic trade, the IBIS index surged 83.35 points or 2.37 percent to 3,599.55.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6937 marks and 113.85 yen compared with 1.6953 marks and 113.80 yen in late European trade on Tuesday.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1300 GMT
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $342.70 compared with $342.75 an ounce at Tuesday's close in London. Silver was down one cent at $4.70.
